title: Hurricanes over warm water, Atlantic 2023
summary: Thirty-one views of the North Atlantic, five days apart from June to October 2023: sea surface temperature, with the track and name of every storm of the season drawn as it happens.
description: Sea surface temperature over the North Atlantic from NASA's MUR analysis (JPL PO DAAC), as drawn by NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio for the 2023 Atlantic hurricane season, on a scale from 20 to 30 degrees Celsius: blue for cooler water, through green and yellow, to red for the warmest. Hurricanes tend to form over water warmer than about 26.5 degrees Celsius. Each storm's track is drawn as a dotted line with its name and its strength (TD tropical depression, TS tropical storm, 1 to 5 hurricane category); the tracks and names come from NOAA's National Weather Service. The app reads the sea's colours as temperatures; the lines, names, land and space count as no data. The view is a fixed globe, so each place stays in one spot. Each frame is the one nearest noon of its day. The numbers are read from the colours, so they are about, not exact.

source.name: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, 2023 Atlantic Hurricane Season (Sea Surface Temperature only; MUR SST, JPL PO DAAC; storm tracks NOAA)

comparisons.question: Which date shows warmer water in the North Atlantic?
comparisons.explanation: Date B (25 August) reads about 29.1 degrees Celsius in the middle colour of the sea; date A (1 June) about 28.4. The sea warms through the summer, the height of the hurricane season. These numbers are read from the colours of the maps, so they are about, not exact.

pairsWith.note: Both cover June to August 2023: the North Atlantic warms into its summer while the sea around Mauritius cools into its southern winter, so the two move in opposite directions.
